source_title: Luckin Coffee Agrees to Pay $180 Million Penalty to Settle Accounting Fraud Charges
company_context: Luckin Coffee Inc. was a fast-growing Chinese coffee retail chain that positioned itself as a Starbucks rival and listed on Nasdaq. The SEC charged it with materially misstating revenue, expenses, and net operating loss to appear to achieve rapid growth and profitability and to meet earnings estimates.
business_type: Coffee retail / restaurant chain (formerly Nasdaq-listed, China)
evidence_summary: From at least April 2019 through January 2020, Luckin intentionally fabricated more than $300 million in retail sales using related parties to create false transactions through three purchasing schemes. Employees concealed the fraud by inflating expenses by more than $190 million, building a fake operations database, and altering accounting and bank records. Luckin settled SEC charges for a $180 million penalty without admitting or denying the allegations. It was delisted from Nasdaq in June 2020, filed Chapter 15 in February 2021, restructured roughly $460M of debt, and emerged from all bankruptcy proceedings on 11 April 2022 — surviving as an operating company.
outcome_evidence: SEC announced the $180 million settlement on 16 December 2020. Luckin was delisted from Nasdaq (June 2020), filed Chapter 15 bankruptcy (Feb 2021), and emerged from all bankruptcy proceedings on 11 April 2022; it continued operating and recovered (later reported as a multi-billion-dollar valuation and exploring U.S. relisting). Outcome sequence: 15 (fraud crisis) then 3 (severe distress but survival).
source_limitations: SEC press-release page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; settlement figures are quoted verbatim from SEC.gov search-result snippets. Survival/emergence details corroborated by Luckin investor relations, SEC EDGAR 6-K (FY2022), Bloomberg Law, and Nasdaq/CNBC reporting.
